question: Which of the following best describes the stored-program (Von Neumann) concept that underlies most modern computers?
optionA: Programs must be physically rewired into the hardware for each new task
optionB: Both program instructions and data are stored in the same memory and can be fetched and modified like any other data
optionC: Instructions are permanently etched onto read-only chips and cannot be changed
optionD: Each instruction requires a separate dedicated processor

optionB: To define the set of instructions, registers, and data types that software can use to interact with the hardware

question: Why do computer systems use a memory hierarchy (registers -> cache -> RAM -> disk) instead of a single type of memory?
optionA: Because a single memory technology cannot simultaneously provide high speed, large capacity, and low cost, so the hierarchy balances these tradeoffs
optionB: Because all memory types are equally fast and this is just a tradition
optionC: Because programs cannot run without multiple memory types
optionD: Because the operating system requires at least four separate memories to boot

question: What is the primary purpose of cache memory in a computer system?
optionA: To permanently store all program data
optionB: To provide a small, fast memory that holds frequently or recently used data, reducing average memory access time
optionC: To replace the need for a hard disk

optionA: To execute only one instruction per program run
optionB: To overlap the execution of multiple instructions in different stages, increasing instruction throughput
optionC: To eliminate the need for registers
optionD: To slow down the clock for safety

question: Which formula correctly relates CPU execution time to instruction count, clock cycles per instruction (CPI), and clock cycle time?
optionA: CPU time = Instruction count / (CPI x Clock cycle time)
optionB: CPU time = Instruction count x CPI x Clock cycle time
optionC: CPU time = Clock cycle time / (Instruction count x CPI)
